s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of bilateral lower limb redness, pain, and swelling with sclerotic plaques in a patient undergoing chemotherapy
salient_findings: Acute onset of redness, pain, and swelling of both lower limbs
Ill-defined, erythematoedematous plaques symmetrically distributed along the shins
key_facts: Patient is a man in his late 70s
Received 4 cycles of chemotherapy with carboplatin, pemetrexed, and pembrolizumab
Currently in maintenance with pemetrexed-pembrolizumab
Edema appeared 5 days after the patient's 8th cycle of chemotherapy
Patient remained afebrile and systemically well
No elevation of inflammatory markers
Normal kidney, liver, and heart functions
Venous Doppler ultrasonography of legs showed no evidence of deep vein thrombosis
Pathology showed thickened dermal collagen with activated fibroblasts and lymphocytic perivascular infiltration

shortlist.label: Chemotherapy-induced scleroderma-like reaction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed sclerotic plaques after chemotherapy

shortlist.label: Erythema nodosum
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of redness, pain, and swelling of lower limbs

shortlist.label: Scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with sclerotic plaques and thickened dermal collagen

shortlist.label: Morphea
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had localized sclerotic plaques and lymphocytic perivascular infiltration

shortlist.label: Lipodermatosclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had induration and erythematous plaques on the lower limbs

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of redness, pain, and swelling of both lower limbs, which evolved into sclerotic plaques, appeared 5 days after the 8th cycle of chemotherapy, and the pathology showed thickened dermal collagen with activated fibroblasts and lymphocytic perivascular infiltration, consistent with a scleroderma-like reaction induced by chemotherapy.

rejected.label: Erythema nodosum
rejected.why: Erythema nodosum typically presents with tender, erythematous nodules, usually on the shins, but the patient's symptoms and pathology results do not fully align with this condition.

rejected.label: Scleroderma
rejected.why: Scleroderma is a chronic autoimmune disease that typically presents with a more gradual onset of symptoms and is not directly linked to chemotherapy.

rejected.label: Morphea
rejected.why: Morphea is a localized form of scleroderma, but the patient's symptoms are more widespread and appeared in conjunction with chemotherapy.

rejected.label: Lipodermatosclerosis
rejected.why: Lipodermatosclerosis is a condition associated with chronic venous insufficiency, but the patient's venous Doppler ultrasonography showed no evidence of deep vein thrombosis, and the pathology results do not support this diagnosis.
